stories.headline: Starmer fights to survive Labour leadership crisis after catastrophic local election losses
stories.summary: Prime Minister Keir Starmer faced the gravest threat to his premiership after Labour's disastrous May 7 local and regional elections, with nearly 90 MPs calling for his resignation, four junior ministers resigning, and Health Secretary Wes Streeting quitting and announcing a leadership bid. Starmer refused to step down, warning a contest would 'plunge the country into chaos,' while Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham secured a by-election path back to parliament and announced his own candidacy, sending gilt yields to their highest since 1998 and prompting international market concern.

stories.headline: Reform UK wins local elections; Farage faces parliamentary probe over £5 million undisclosed gift
stories.summary: Reform UK emerged as the dominant winner of the May 7 local elections, gaining approximately 1,400 council seats across England. Simultaneously, parliamentary standards watchdog launched an investigation into Nigel Farage for failing to declare a £5 million gift from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne; Farage later described the money as 'a reward for campaigning for Brexit.' Elon Musk publicly accused Farage of lying about the incident.

stories.headline: King Charles delivers King's Speech at State Opening of Parliament amid Starmer leadership turmoil
stories.summary: King Charles III presided over the State Opening of Parliament on May 13, delivering the government's legislative agenda including 37 bills, among them a Tackling State Threats Bill and new antisemitism measures. Buckingham Palace had privately raised with No. 10 whether the ceremony should proceed given Starmer's precarious position; it went ahead with David Lammy handing Charles the speech in an unusual break from protocol.

stories.headline: Far-right Tommy Robinson march and pro-Palestine demonstration draw tens of thousands to London with 11 arrests
stories.summary: Two major protests converged on London on May 16: Tommy Robinson's 'Unite the Kingdom' rally and a pro-Palestine Nakba Day march. Around 4,000 police officers were deployed with armoured vehicles, dogs, and drones; 11 people were arrested. Deputy PM David Lammy condemned the far-right organisers as 'spreading hatred and division' and warned of swift action if violence occurred.

stories.headline: Bank of England softens stablecoin regulatory framework after industry pushback
stories.summary: Bank of England Deputy Governor Sarah Breeden signalled that the central bank was reconsidering its proposed stablecoin framework, including temporary ownership caps of £20,000 per individual and 40% reserve requirements, describing earlier proposals as potentially 'overly conservative.' The BoE also signalled openness to sterling stablecoin issuers ahead of the FCA regime coming into force, aiming to keep London competitive against US and European digital asset markets.

stories.headline: King Charles visits Golders Green in solidarity with Jewish community after antisemitic attacks
stories.summary: King Charles III visited a Jewish community centre in the north London neighbourhood of Golders Green on May 14, meeting victims of a stabbing attack and members of the Shomrim emergency response service following an unprecedented wave of antisemitic violence in the UK. Chief Rabbi Ephraim Mirvis and Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mark Rowley accompanied the King.

stories.headline: Rachel Reeves highlights UK GDP growth while warning leadership contest risks economic recovery
stories.summary: UK GDP grew 0.6% in Q1 2026, beating forecasts and boosting Chancellor Rachel Reeves's position ahead of any Labour leadership transition. Reeves publicly warned that a contest would 'plunge the country into chaos at a time of economic risk,' withdrew from public engagements to lobby MPs for Starmer, and also faced Conservative attacks over a proposed tourism levy.

One of Lammy's parliamentary aides, Melanie Ward, resigned from her position, adding to the pressure.

stories.headline: Bank of England monetary policy: rate-setters divided as Iran war energy shock clouds outlook
stories.summary: Bank of England MPC members gave conflicting signals on rate direction this week. Deputy Governor Breeden said hikes were not needed in June or July; hawkish member Catherine Mann warned a future shock could trigger gilt market instability as overseas investors replace domestic pension funds; MPC member Megan Greene said it was worth waiting to assess the Iran war's economic impact before backing hikes. The Bank's governor had previously flagged a 'very big energy shock' from the conflict.

stories.headline: Bank of England and Treasury warn financial firms on frontier AI cyber threats
stories.summary: The Bank of England, Financial Conduct Authority, and HM Treasury issued a joint statement urging regulated financial firms to strengthen cyber defences against threats posed by frontier AI models including Anthropic's Mythos and ChatGPT 5.5 Instant. The PRA's head separately warned of 'quite significant disruption' to financial services from advanced AI models.

stories.headline: Lammy meets UAE foreign minister over Iran attacks on UAE; Farage also granted unusual diplomatic meeting
stories.summary: UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed met UK Deputy PM David Lammy in London to discuss Iran's drone and missile attacks on civilian sites in the UAE. In an unusual diplomatic signal, the UAE minister separately met Reform UK leader Nigel Farage, with analysts noting this indicated the UAE treating Farage as a 'prime minister-in-waiting.'
